approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES prior on the supplied unlabeled strings, then chooses a checkpoint with a fixed holdout. Each objective receives a fresh policy copy and a frozen reference prior. Its best current observations train together with a uniform sample from the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted scores. A fixed prior-likelihood-plus-reward target drives bounded policy updates, and ancestral sampling generates complete new molecules that pass chemical and duplicate checks. Every unlabeled molecule is always presented in the same supplied traversal, so alternative starts and attachment contexts of that molecule receive no direct training exposure.
approach.novelty: Add equivalent rooted-SMILES views only during unlabeled prior training. For each selected training molecule, choose between its original string and one cached alternate traversal rooted at a reproducibly selected atom. Verify that the alternate has exactly the same canonical molecular identity and fits the existing token interface before using it. This lets the same molecular connections appear in different sequence contexts while preserving the original fixed holdout and all online learning rules. The earlier sibling grouped bracket characters into atom units; this experiment retains the Parent tokenizer and instead tests invariance to molecular traversal. Any improved language coverage must still transfer to valid novel chemistry to count as useful search.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-15499bde2e65 trains its prior on one supplied serialization per unlabeled corpus row and its accepted replay on exact original strings; neither preparation nor online learning offers an equivalent traversal view. Its actual three-seed generation logs contain 10,528 duplicate draws among 34,960 raw draws, although all announced batches complete. The Molecular assessment describes broad scaffold coverage but uneven preservation of useful attachment and nitrogen-functional-state relationships. These observations motivate testing serialization-context dependence; they do not prove that canonical-view training caused concentration. The Parent three-seed macro mean is 0.5075540530185733. Sibling n-40b80eb7455d confirmed bracket-unit representation learning, improved bracket-bearing holdout likelihood and reduced aggregate invalidity, yet its paired macro change was -0.0009832613721652932 and bracket-bearing accepted proposals fell from 1,269 to 835. Thus better local token modeling alone has not supplied the expected optimization benefit. A read-only probe of 1,000 allowed corpus rows using the Parent prepared seed and inherited tokenizer produced 965 different rooted strings, with zero canonical/isomeric identity mismatches and zero length exclusions; this establishes a usable view mechanism on that probe, not a score effect or corpus-wide guarantee.
hypothesis: During unlabeled prior training, mix each selected molecule's supplied SMILES with one cached, deterministic atom-rooted SMILES view whose canonical/isomeric molecular identity is verified, exposing the unchanged recurrent model to equivalent attachment contexts while keeping online learning and sampling unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Rooted views learned equivalent traversals, but validity fell and one replica stopped early
finding_summary.insights: Equivalent traversal exposure reached the training loss and transferred to held-out alternative strings. The smaller serialization preference is supported by improved alternate likelihood, while the loss on the supplied strings makes the tradeoff visible. This narrows the bottleneck: adding sequence contexts can improve traversal coverage without delivering reliable chemical search improvement. Lower duplicate rates did not translate into broader accepted scaffold coverage; invalid draws increased and late chemical families became more concentrated. The chemistry still favors conventional aromatic amine and carbonyl families, with unresolved attachment placement, extreme-size tails and reactive outliers. No missing stereochemical information was recovered. The available score changes are mixed and the completed-seed mean gain is below the registered 0.002 effect; the failed third task prevents the full intended score comparison. The specific canonicalization key mismatch identifies a separate robustness gap in the inherited feedback interface. Preparation stayed within the existing deadline and retained the same number of training batches, so lost training steps do not explain this outcome. Whether improved equivalent-string likelihood can preserve original-string quality and improve useful chemical coverage remains open.
finding_summary.results: Across three preparations, changed equivalent views appeared 10,938,511 times and contributed 553,572,420 target tokens to real training batches. Reconstructing all 3,629,346 cached row/view pairs and every training tensor receipt found no identity, token round-trip, length, or holdout-membership violation. The fixed panels contained 11,774 changed views. Their alternate NLL fell from 4.5739 to 0.7043 nats per alternate token. Under the same independent checkpoint comparison, alternate NLL improved from the parent's 1.6256 to 0.7043, while original-string NLL worsened from 0.5638 to 0.6004. The alternate-minus-original full-sequence NLL gap narrowed from 55.16 to 6.61 nats per changed molecule. Each preparation finished 29,742 training batches; mean preparation time rose from 243.5 to 902.0 seconds, with a 401.8 MiB temporary cache. On the same 14 completed tasks, raw validity fell from 90.24% to 86.55%, duplicates fell from 29.22% to 23.47%, and novel draws rose from 61.01% to 63.08%. Mean accepted scaffold counts stayed similar (218.4 to 217.2), while late scaffold concentration increased. The two completed paired seeds scored 0.51444 versus 0.51394, a mean change of +0.00050; their individual changes were -0.00199 and +0.00300. The third DRD2 run stopped at 170 evaluations because an emitted aromatic string changed canonical form when reparsed, activating the unchanged feedback-provenance guard. Its incomplete task leaves the three-seed macro score unavailable. All logged online updates preserve the frozen prior and original accepted replay strings.

molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic amines and carbonyl heterocycles dominate, with size extremes and an anomalous oxygen cation
molecular.overall_character: The output spans many recognizable medicinal-chemistry families: diarylamino heteroarenes, substituted quinazolines and pyrimidinones, indole-linked piperazines, sulfonamides, hydantoins, ureas and small saturated rings. Most leading molecules are medium-sized and have conventional bonds, with plausible synthetic entry points through amide formation, amine substitution or aromatic coupling. The full trajectories are structurally broad, although individual late families become much narrower. The supplied digest contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task except drd2_docking, which has 770 molecules and 740 proposals; that task's seed-2 trajectory ends at evaluation 170, so no later molecules are inferred. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9816 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9483 to 0.9966. Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.2 to 50.1, but long polyaryl assemblies, lipids, peptides and highly polar nucleotide-like structures create an extreme-size tail. Charged-token rates range from 0.023 to 0.1207; many charges belong to recognizable nitro or N-oxide groups, while a leading molecule contains a chemically anomalous terminal positive oxygen. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the supplied parent strings. The overall chemistry is mostly plausible and moderately drug-like, with isolated severe exceptions and no evidence that all stereogenic products represent defined stereoisomers.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leading family consists of fairly compact diarylamino pyrimidines or a related pyridine, decorated with methoxy, ethoxy, methyl, phenol and aryl halogen groups. These are aromatic, largely flat molecules with exocyclic NH connections and heteroaromatic acceptors. Most of this family has ordinary, synthetically plausible bonding. The best-scoring entry is an exception: its terminal positive oxygen is singly attached to an aryl carbon and has an open-shell valence representation, rather than an ordinary phenol or ether. Other seeds contain acylurea and hydrazone-related aromatic families. The lowest examples are much larger polyaryl assemblies, elaborate fused polycycles or long unsaturated chains with multiple carbonyl groups.
liabilities: The singly bound terminal positive oxygen in the nominal best entry is an unusual open-shell species and cannot be treated as an ordinary stable medicinal substituent.
Multiple aromatic rings and aryl NH links yield predominantly flat structures, while the extreme tail adds excessive ring and linker complexity.
Hydrazone-related and heavily elaborated low-scoring molecules introduce additional configurational or chemical ambiguity without resolving the observed structural fit.
missing_features: The large low-scoring structures lack the compact aromatic and polar-group arrangement retained by the neutral diarylamino heteroarene leaders.
Matched neutral, closed-shell alternatives around the best oxygen-cation entry are not fully established by the displayed examples, although closely scoring ordinary phenolic relatives already exist.

The current leading set does not recover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule; this is a missing well-performing chemical family among the displayed leaders, not proof that a particular group is universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The unusual oxygen-cation structure scores 0.42762099872850584, while ordinary phenol/methoxy/methyl diarylamino pyrimidines with either meta aryl chlorine or fluorine score 0.42408253349563446. Ethoxy analogues score 0.42036761694214836 for either halogen, so the chemical family is supported without relying on the anomalous oxygen. Moving chlorine from the meta to para position in the displayed phenol-containing series gives 0.3925552460025089; the para-hydroxy relative scores 0.342125381162771. The largest multiaryl example scores 8.434866188027838e-50. This favors a compact arrangement of aromatic rings, amino links and selected substituent positions, rather than indiscriminate aromatic growth. Parent seed 0 reached 0.5280588545286916 with a compact substituted indole carboxamide; current seed 0 reaches 0.40822403535979507 with an acylurea-like family. Current seed 2 instead reaches 0.42762099872850584 versus the parent's 0.3900700429110833 with an aryl sulfonamide family. These different frameworks leave no unique missing pharmacophore established.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are moderately sized to bulky, aromatic and heteroaromatic structures with methoxy-rich phenyl or fused aza-aromatic systems. Quinazoline-like cores carry amidine, amide or aryl connections; another strong family consists of amino pyrimidinones connecting a methoxylated aryl group to a fluorinated aryl or pyridyl group. The amide, amidine, amino and ether functionality is mostly conventional and synthetically plausible. Some other high examples link several nitrogen-rich heterocycles, increasing aromatic density. The lows include a small acyclic polyether, simple dimethoxybenzene, a small bicyclic lactam and sulfur-oxidized aromatic compounds.
liabilities: Repeated aromatic and methoxy-rich substitution creates fairly flat, heavily decorated structures with limited saturated shape diversity in the leading series.
Amidine protonation and the ionization of nitrogen-rich heterocycles are not characterized by their mostly neutral drawn forms.
Large multiheteroaryl extensions and occasional reactive or charged structures in the wider trajectory add chemistry outside the relatively conventional leading families.
missing_features: Small fragment-like products lack the connected multi-ring heteroaromatic and polar-linker organization present in the leading molecules.

The low-scoring sulfone relatives show that adding an acceptor-rich substituent does not preserve the needed arrangement. More matched changes in linker position, heteroaromatic nitrogen placement and substitution are needed to distinguish useful geometry from mere group presence.

The displayed high-scoring series offers relatively little saturated-ring shape variation while retaining its useful aromatic and polar fragments; these data do not establish whether that missing shape diversity would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amidine-bearing methoxy-rich aza-aromatic molecule scores 0.6070600130851127, versus 0.601092340050207 for its amide relative. A trifluoroanilide aza-aromatic compound scores 0.6051953628166595 and an amino pyrimidinone with a fluoropyridyl group reaches 0.6038062283737025. Simple fragments score 0.500879275477007 to 0.50171998624011. Sulfone-bearing examples score 0.26359367276322293, 0.28248974008207933 and 0.3089070855614973 despite retaining recognizable chemistry. Thus the observed gradient rewards a particular multi-ring heteroaromatic and polar-linker organization more clearly than aromatic content or synthetic plausibility alone. Current seed-1 and seed-2 families reach 0.6070600130851127 and 0.6038062283737025, compared with parental 0.61192894944948 and 0.5758665324320438; the latter parent used a sulfur-containing fused carbonyl framework. The comparison does not establish a general prohibition on sulfur.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are conventional indoles joined through short alkyl chains to an aryl-substituted piperazine. Their substituents include aryl chlorine or nitrile, alkoxy, alkyl, alkenyl, alkynyl and ordinary thioether groups. They combine an indole NH, an available aliphatic amine and substantial aromatic surface. Seed 0 also supplies substituted piperidine/benzylamine frameworks, while the observed seed-2 endpoint is a pyrrole-containing aryl diaza-ring compound. These families are generally synthetically plausible and are much closer to ordinary medicinal chemistry than the low amide, sulfonamide or nitroso-containing examples. The seed-2 assessment covers only the supplied evaluations through 170.
liabilities: Flexible alkyl links, hydrophobic substituents and several aromatic rings accumulate in the leading family; similar scores across these variants do not show a need for every appendage.
Thioethers, alkenes and alkynes provide chemically plausible but distinct stability and metabolism profiles that the observed scores do not resolve.
An N-nitroso-containing ring appears in the low-scoring tail, and amide-rich unrelated structures often lose the freely basic amine organization.
missing_features: The low amide and sulfonamide examples lack an accessible aliphatic amine in the aromatic-linker arrangement present in the leading family.

Matched alternatives that separate linker geometry, aromatic substitution and amine identity are not fully represented by the displayed leaders; their nearly equal scores provide no basis for inventing a uniquely required extra group.
The main indole/piperazine leaders need no tetrahedral stereochemical assignment, but other substituted saturated-ring families in the trajectories leave possible stereogenic centres unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading indole/alkyl/piperazine molecule scores 0.9999999860118697; methoxy, nitrile, methyl, alkene and alkyne relatives also have scores close to 1.0. A shorter alkyl connection still scores 0.9999990128281356. This strongly associates the observed high scores with the linked aromatic/aliphatic-amine framework, but the very small differences among these leaders do not identify a necessary peripheral substituent. A sulfonylated pyrrolidine carboxamide scores 2.4886239921722126e-05, and other amide-dominated molecules remain very low. The initial molecules likewise show that nitrogen content alone is insufficient. Parent seed 1 already had an indole/alkyl/arylpiperazine leader at 0.9999999999666845. The present highest family retains that broad chemistry with different decoration. The observed seed-2 endpoint scores 0.9999887250097366; its shorter trajectory is not treated as a complete three-seed endpoint comparison.

per_task.generated_character: The leading chemistry includes compact arylsulfonyl piperazines, especially a phenylsulfonyl piperazine bearing a benzodioxole-methyl substituent. Smaller N-methyl arylsulfonyl piperazines also recur. Other leading examples add fused aromatic rings, a cyclic imide or a lactone-containing sulfonyl partner. These combine ordinary sulfonamide, ether/acetal-like benzodioxole and aliphatic amine functionality and are mostly synthetically plausible. Low examples include small polar acyclic fragments, a highly hydroxylated cyclohexane, a long-chain carbonyl/sulfinic-acid structure and a largely hydrocarbon polycycle. The final seed-2 molecules return to fused heteroaromatic and benzodioxole-rich structures with uneven scores.
liabilities: Benzodioxole and aromatic substitution are conventional but heavily reused among the better examples, limiting the variety of closely matched alternatives.
The low tail spans both excessive hydrocarbon content and strongly polar fragment-like structures, losing the balance present in the compact leaders.
Stereogenic polyols and complex spiro or fused-ring alternatives have no explicit stereochemical assignments, though the principal piperazine leader is not dependent on a tetrahedral stereocentre.
missing_features: The very low-scoring polyols, small polar fragments and hydrocarbon-rich structures lack the combined aromatic, sulfonyl and amine organization of the leading family.

Many relatives contain only part of the useful fragment combination or add larger fused systems without improving the observed score. More matched arrangements of the same fragments are missing from the compact leading series.

The trajectories do not establish a specific additional pharmacophore beyond those observed associations; the remaining gap is coverage of compatible geometry and connectivity rather than a simple absent atom type.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The combined phenylsulfonyl-piperazine/benzodioxole-methyl molecule scores 0.23462432156460183. Replacing its phenylsulfonyl substituent by methyl gives 0.20456947096636482, while the phenylsulfonyl piperazine carrying methyl on the other nitrogen scores 0.20718664161756667. This supports the combined aromatic, sulfonyl and amine arrangement rather than either fragment alone. Small or differently organized polar compounds score 0.01951057027596422 to 0.0373568506471187, so polarity or ring content alone is insufficient. A more elaborate aza-ring relative reaches 0.21742081989615164, below the simpler leading combination. Parent seed 0 reached 0.20090425134085538 with a benzodioxole-containing heteroaromatic carbonyl structure; the current leading sulfonyl piperazine is chemically different. Current seed 1 and seed 2 reach 0.20779009147462646 and 0.19293590828532245 versus parental 0.21944544104637362 and 0.20718664161756667, leaving a mixed comparison.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family comprises fluorinated aryl hydantoins with an additional acetamide side chain, giving compact nitrogen/carbonyl rings, NH donors and aromatic fluorine. Other high examples include a gem-difluorocyclobutane bearing carboxylic acid and benzylurea groups, and a fluorobenzylamino purine with a cyclobutanol substituent. These are distinct, mostly conventional synthetic families; a conjugated cyano/sulfone/carbonyl ring is another alternative. The worst molecules are much larger long-chain lipids, highly polar phosphate-rich nucleotide-like structures or peptide-like assemblies. Many final seed-2 molecules are ordinary small aromatic amides and heterocycles but score very poorly, showing that plausible chemistry alone is insufficient.
liabilities: The wider output contains extreme hydrophobic long chains and highly polar phosphate or peptide assemblies, both far from the moderate size of the leading structures.
Multiple carbonyls, NH groups and a carboxylic acid in some leaders create substantial polarity; the purine alternative shows that the useful chemical balance is family-dependent.
Unspecified stereochemistry and alkene geometry remain in saturated-ring and conjugated alternatives.
missing_features: Low-scoring large molecules and generic aromatic amides lack the compact, specifically spaced polar and fluorinated-carbon arrangement of the displayed stronger families.

Hydantoin analogues with altered aryl fluorination or amide spacing show that preserving functional-group identity without its placement is insufficient; more matched fluorine-position and linker variants would clarify the remaining gap.
The substituted hydantoin and cyclobutanol families leave possible absolute or relative stereochemistry unassigned. No stereospecific requirement can be inferred from the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated aryl hydantoin with a fluorobenzyl acetamide scores 0.37576103635478436. Removing the benzyl methylene gives 0.3350386388148056, and removing fluorine from the hydantoin-bound phenyl group gives 0.2767352716721542. These matched comparisons support specific fluorine placement and linker spacing within this family. A different gem-difluorocyclobutane acid/urea reaches 0.35652091248579093 and the purine/cyclobutanol family reaches 0.34452496576406605, so a carbonyl-rich ring is not universally required by the observed data. The largest lipids, phosphate-rich and peptide-like structures score 0.0; the task median is 0.000001. Current seed-0 and seed-1 maxima exceed the parent's 0.2932061327730367 and 0.28770317918999355 while using different chemical families, but current seed 2 reaches only 0.2411316843576229 versus parental 0.3108657757276207. These associations do not reveal a unique hidden target structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading aromatic amine structure contains a singly bound terminal positive oxygen and scores 0.42762099872850584, while ordinary phenolic relatives score 0.42408253349563446. Charge-token rates alone do not distinguish this anomaly from ordinary nitro and N-oxide groups elsewhere in the proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: Occasional open-shell or incompletely valenced charged fragments survive alongside otherwise conventional medicinal chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve chemically appropriate valence, hydrogen count and electronic state when changing atom identity or charge. Supply stable closed-shell alternatives around useful molecular frameworks without excluding legitimate charged functional groups.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tail includes giant multiaryl assemblies, long hydrocarbon chains, peptide-like molecules, phosphate-rich nucleotide-like structures and small polar fragments lacking the aromatic and linker organization of the stronger examples. The better examples instead retain compact aromatic/amine, sulfonyl/amine or fluorinated/polar arrangements; some extreme molecules have recorded scores of 0.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still emits extreme sizes and polarities that lose the organization found in its better molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer changes that preserve a useful scale and local functional-group balance while varying molecular shape. Avoid making a local chemical change depend on large scaffold accretion, long-chain growth or removal of most of the relevant framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Moving an aryl substituent changes a displayed aromatic-amine score from 0.42408253349563446 to 0.3925552460025089. Removing a benzyl methylene changes a carbonyl-ring analogue from 0.37576103635478436 to 0.3350386388148056. Combining a benzodioxole-methyl group with a phenylsulfonyl piperazine gives 0.23462432156460183 versus lower scores for relatives retaining only part of that arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of matched functional-group positions and linker geometry remains incomplete despite clear local score differences.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate chemically coherent matched series that vary substituent position, linker length, heteroaromatic nitrogen placement and ring shape while retaining the other useful fragments. Let observed scores determine which arrangements matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited hydantoins, cyclobutanol derivative, polyols and complex spiro or fused alternatives contain possible stereogenic relationships, whereas many leading flat heteroarenes and simple piperazines are naturally achiral.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic saturated-ring products lack explicit stereochemical identities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible absolute and relative configurations where stereochemistry exists, and generate matched stereoisomers when relevant. Apply this to genuinely stereogenic structures rather than treating stereochemical labels as a universal molecular feature.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
